notes: The post-quantum key exchange is now genuinely ML-KEM-1024 (FIPS 203). Earlier releases performed Kyber-1024, the NIST round-3 candidate ML-KEM was standardised from, while describing it as ML-KEM-1024 - the two are different algorithms and do not interoperate. The stated algorithm and the performed algorithm now match, and the key exchange no longer accepts a weaker parameter set. Video call frames are now protected against tampering as well as against reading. Each device generates fresh keys on first launch and registers as a new device; messages sent before this release cannot be opened afterwards, and no Vault file is affected.
